title: Suggestions for 3D model generation?
author: anakingentefina
selftext:
Hi guys, I am building a cozy game, very polygonal lol but Codex Astra is not up to the task yet, my last character had a very uncommon look >:(

What and how are you guys using to generate assets?

  
TYSM <3

comments.author: Ukawok92
comments.body: You could also look on Sketchfab for 3D models with a CC0 or similar license.

replies.author: anakingentefina
replies.body: Taking a look, thanks. But I would still want to do some more customizable ones.

comments.author: zjgkkn
comments.body:
I don’t quite get the aesthetic behind an approach where an LLM builds something in Blender using basic primitives.

For generation, the easiest route is to use services like Tripo or Meshy. If you need to generate assets locally, ComfyUI seems like a solid choice.

Ultimately, you could even build your own studio -- LLMs are perfectly capable of handling that. For instance, here’s mine: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets\_studio](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets_studio)

replies.author: anakingentefina
replies.body: thats pretty cool, gonna take a look

comments.author: No-Association-1834
comments.body: If you have decent GPU , install Unreal Engine and use Meta Human , it is one way to get good Characters . Of you have Blender - MPFB Makehuman addon works to easily create characters ,but not that great looking . 3rd would be Sketchfab , Cgtrader , Polyhaven CC0 downloads , you can also put Custom Paid Request on CGTRADER , and someone will build the character for you if you have the concept or image .

comments.author: redth
comments.body:
I’ve had luck with meshy.ai. My workflow has roughly been generate an image of what I want first with it and then use the image in the prompt to get a 3d model of it. 

The main issue is this produces very random texture maps that you really can’t reason about editing them flat. 

What has been useful is to use this for placeholders while building the game and then hiring someone to make a real version of what I want with better rigging and a human touch. It helps give them a good sense of the style I want.

replies.author: pol-delta
replies.body: How much does hiring somebody cost? I’ve gotten decent results for models from Meshy or Tripo – or sometimes Claude actually does a better job, but mostly not. But for animations, they’re all (Meshy/Claude/Codex) falling short for me.

replies.author: redth
replies.body:
Depends on many things of course but I’ve been happy with someone I’ve been working with on a couple models. The main first humanoid model with rigging and textures and some poses was a few hundred.

But I also really want to involve humans more in the artistic parts of what I’m building, so that has value to me.

comments.author: jildos_legoplanet
comments.body: Meshy works pretty well if you have the right example images. I ask Codex to generate me first a concept image from front 1/4 side. Then use that as a reference for Orthogonal (0 perspective) from straight front/right/left and back. Do check for symmetry!

comments.author: olafthemanofsnow
comments.body: Meshy is reasonably good for model generation
